chain.label: Inadequate smoke/fire detection certification standards
chain.trigger: cargo compartment smoke detection certification tests...were not conducted with cargo loaded on the airplane

chain.label: No requirement for on-board cargo fire suppression system
chain.trigger: the airplane was not required to be equipped with a fire suppression system

chain.label: No specific checklist guidance for unalerted smoke/fumes
chain.trigger: The UPS DC-8 Aircraft Operating Manual does not contain specific procedures on how to respond to in-flight smoke, fire, or fumes in the absence of a cockpit warning

chain.label: PHL ARFF lacked cargo aircraft familiarization/HRET training
chain.trigger: PHL did not schedule cargo aircraft familiarization training, including training on the operation of the doors of the aircraft used by UPS

chain.label: Smoldering fire ignites in cargo container 12, 13, or 14 from an unknown source
chain.trigger: an in-flight cargo fire that initiated from an unknown source, which was most likely located within cargo container 12, 13, or 14

chain.label: Crew executes Fumes Evacuation checklist, diluting smoke and feeding fire oxygen
chain.trigger: the flight engineer stated that he set the air conditioning packs to maximum flow and turned off the recirculation fan

caused_by.evidence: the AOM did not provide guidance on when to use the [Fumes Evacuation] checklist
the first officer asking the captain and the flight engineer if they detected an odor that smelled 'like wood burning'

chain.label: Crew declares emergency, lands on runway 27R, and evacuates via L1 slide
chain.trigger: the first officer called for an emergency evacuation...All of the flight crewmembers successfully evacuated the airplane using the emergency slide

caused_by.evidence: the flight engineer stated, 'we got cargo smoke'...requested that emergency response equipment meet them upon landing
The increased airflow that resulted from the Fumes Evacuation checklist actions diluted the smoke and inhibited its detection...and provided the fire with additional oxygen

chain.label: ARFF personnel unable to promptly open cargo door or pierce fuselage
chain.trigger: Several attempts were made by ARFF personnel to open the main cargo door...Subsequent attempts...were also unsuccessful

caused_by.evidence: PHL ARFF personnel experienced problems opening the main cargo door during the emergency response

chain.label: Airplane and most cargo destroyed by fire; crew sustains minor injuries
chain.trigger: The airplane was destroyed by fire after landing...flight crewmembers sustained minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: The airplane was destroyed by fire after landing
the airplane was not required to be equipped with a fire suppression system, and, as a result, the fire...was able to develop into a substantial fire
PHL ARFF personnel were not familiar with the accident airplane's main cargo door, which adversely affected their ability to access the airplane's interior to fight the fire
